source_text: Me - affirmas - aliter intellegere, quam totum ipsum capitulum debet intellegi
pass_a_gloss: Me - affirmas - aliter intellegere, than/which whole itself capitulum ought to-be-understood.
pass_b_english: You understand the apostle’s words differently from the way that entire passage ought to be understood: ‘I know that good does not dwell in me, that is, in my flesh,’ through ‘Miserable man that I am! Who will free me from the body of this death?’ (Romans 7:18–24)
Augustine also reports that Julian acknowledges the glorious struggles the saints undertake against the movements of fleshly desire.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

bible_refs.note: Linked from Julian's wording or a clear allusion in the excerpt.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded. This row is Augustine's report; Pass A glosses only the Julian words recoverable here.
